CHIEF COMPLAINT
Post-operative follow-up for bilateral reduction mammoplasty

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
36-year-old female status post bilateral reduction mammoplasty on 10-10-2020. Patient reports her breasts are doing great and she is no longer experiencing back pain. She is overall doing well and enjoying summertime. During a prior visit with PA Ruth Sanchez in March, a lump was noted under the left breast, but patient has not palpated this since that visit and has been performing massages. Patient noted scars were bothering her and obtained scar gel which she has been using daily, though states she doesn't think she needs it now.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chills, fever, nausea, or vomiting. Denies back pain. Denies noticing hard spots, lumps, or bumps.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Bilateral reduction mammoplasty (10-10-2020)

MEDICATIONS
Mederma scar gel - using daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Enjoying summertime. Family doing well.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Breasts: Incisions are well healed with no signs of infection or redness on either breast. Some scar widening noted bilaterally, particularly in high-tension areas. Previously noted lump under left breast is not palpated on current examination. Patient healing well overall.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Status post bilateral reduction mammoplasty with good post-operative healing and well-healed incisions without signs of infection.
2. Scar widening noted bilaterally in high-tension areas.
3. Continue Mederma scar gel twice daily with massage to affected scars.
4. Discussed potential revision by excision and re-closure; patient declines at this time.
5. Follow-up appointment in 6 months to reassess scars. Noted that revision surgery will not be performed until at least 1 year post-operative.
6. Photographs obtained today for documentation and comparison.
